chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who died and appointed an executor, and he had a young son. The boy reached adulthood and went to the executor, saying to him, 'Return my wealth to me so that I may marry.' But he refused him. So he went and committed adultery. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Two-thirds of the sin of the adultery of this man is upon that executor, because he prevented the wealth from him and did not give it to him, so he could have married.'

key_terms.الْوَصِيِّ: The executor or trustee appointed to manage the estate

ai.seo_question: What is the sin of an executor who withholds an heir's inheritance?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the concept of 'sababiyyah' (causality) in Shia jurisprudence, where the executor’s unjust retention of the orphan’s wealth is deemed the primary cause of his subsequent sin of adultery. The specific 2/3 to 1/3 distribution of sin highlights the scholar’s view that the withholding party bears the greater moral weight for creating the condition that led to the transgression, a principle often discussed in commentaries on the rights of orphans (al-yatim).

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from the one who reported it,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who died and bequeathed to a man (to be an executor), and for him was a young son. So the boy became an adult, and went to the executor, so he said to him, ‘Return to me my wealth so that I can get married. But he refused him. So he went and committed adultery’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Two-thirds of the sin of the adultery of this man is upon the executor because he prevented the wealth from him, and did not give it, so he could have got married’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from those who narrated to him who has narrated the following: “This is about the case of a man who dies, with a will to a man, leaving behind a small son who becomes mature. He goes to the executor of the will asking him to handover to him his assets so he can marry. However, the executor of the will refuses and he goes to fornicate. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Two-thirds of the sins of fornication is upon the executor of the will because of his refusal to handover to him his assets so he can marry.’”
